title: $K$-Theoretic Obstructions to Linearizing QCA Representations
abstract: Projective representations arise naturally in physics and representation theory, and determining whether they can be linearized has been a fundamental problem. In this work, we study the analogous problem for quantum cellular automata (QCA) representations, which incorporate locality constraints imposed by a metric space $X$. Over an arbitrary field $\mathbb{F}$, we develop an obstruction theory for the linearization of QCA representations, using the algebraic $K$-theory spectrum of QCA constructed in previous work of the authors. The resulting obstructions are governed by the homotopy type of the QCA spaces, from which we extract universal obstruction classes to linearization. In the complex algebraic and unitary case, we also fully compute the homotopy types of the QCA spaces over a point, a line, and a plane.
summary: This paper develops an advanced obstruction theory using K-theory to determine when Quantum Cellular Automata (QCA) representations can be linearized into standard linear group actions. By analyzing universal obstruction classes derived from the homotopy type of QCA spaces, it establishes precise mathematical criteria for physical systems modeled by QCA to possess simple, linear dynamics.
main_problem: The central problem is developing an obstruction theory to determine when a Quantum Cellular Automata (QCA) representation, which models quantum spin systems with locality constraints, can be linearized into a standard linear group representation.
main_result: The authors establish that the linearizability of QCA representations is governed by the vanishing of specific universal obstruction classes derived from algebraic K-theory spectra. They provide explicit conditions for this vanishing in various settings (e.g., finite groups, rational coefficients).
method: The methodology heavily employs advanced algebraic topology, specifically utilizing stable homotopy theory, K-theory spectra, and cohomology theories to construct and analyze obstruction cocycles.
model_or_system: The model is the QCA representation $\varphi: G 	o Q(X, q)$, where $G$ is a group acting on quantum spin systems defined over a metric space $X$. The locality constraints are encoded in the structure of the algebra of local observables $A(X, q)$.
key_observables: Universal obstruction classes ($u_i(\varphi)$), stabilization maps ($\varphi_{st}$), and specific cohomology/homotopy groups (e.g., $	ext{H}^k(X; \mathbb{F}_p)$, $\pi_i(	ext{K}(C(X)))$).
important_parameters: The field of coefficients ($\mathbb{F}$, $\mathbb{Q}$), the structure of the metric space $X$ (e.g., point, line, plane, lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$), and the group $G$.
main_assumptions: The theory relies on establishing equivalences between different notions of linearizability (linearizable vs. stably linearizable) and assuming certain algebraic properties for the underlying spaces $X$ and groups $G$ (e.g., $G$ being rationally acyclic).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate specific examples of QCA ($\alpha$) associated with central simple algebras or annular shifts on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, used to demonstrate non-circuit, non-linearizable cases.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the single-particle case (Theorem 1.1) to generalizing the obstruction theory for QCA representations over arbitrary fields. It systematically defines various notions of linearizability and derives necessary and sufficient conditions using K-theoretic obstructions across different coefficient rings ($\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{R}$, finite fields).
why_interesting: This work provides a deep mathematical framework connecting quantum computation models (QCA) to fundamental algebraic topology invariants. The explicit calculation of obstruction classes over number fields suggests powerful, non-trivial constraints on physically realizable quantum dynamics.
